title: Latitude and longitude
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers latitude and longitude; bearings and elevation is a related idea about directions and angles, but it does not teach locating places by degrees from the equator and prime meridian.

draft.title: Latitude and longitude
card: measures degrees north or south of the equator. The equator is 0°, and the poles are 90° N and 90° S.
measures degrees east or west of the prime meridian, which runs through Greenwich in London. The prime meridian is 0°, and longitude goes up to 180° E and 180° W.
Latitude is written first, then longitude. Together they give the position of a place, such as Sydney at about 34° S, 151° E.
Lines of latitude run east to west, and each one is a circle around the Earth. Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
draft.remember: Latitude is the angle north or south. Longitude is the angle east or west.

a.q: Which place is in the southern hemisphere and east of the prime meridian?
a.why: S means south of the equator and E means east of the prime meridian. 34° N is north of the equator. 34° S, 151° W is south but west of Greenwich, so it fails the second test.
a.clue: Check the letter after each number.

b.q: Priya reads a map for a town at 37° S, 145° E. What does the 145° E tell her?
opts: It is 145° of longitude east of the prime meridian
It is 145° of latitude east of the prime meridian
It is 145° of longitude east of the equator
It is 145° of latitude north of the equator
b.why: The second number in a position is the longitude, and E means east of the prime meridian. Longitude is not measured from the equator: that is the starting line for latitude.
b.clue: Which line is longitude measured from, and which comes second?

b.best: It is 145° of longitude east of the prime meridian
